transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Before I finalize and publish tomorrow's satellite terminal schedule for the four data sessions, I need to confirm a few things. Do any of the scheduled users — the weather-data feed, the logistics-tracking system, the clinic teleconsult, or the operations status update — have specific terminal compatibility requirements or preferred time blocks I should be aware of? Also, are there any known constraints on SAT-A or SAT-B that would affect which sessions they can support?

transcript.text: Maj. Mercer, the clinic teleconsult requires SAT-A. I confirmed with the clinic technician this morning that the consulting network's current access credential is loaded only on SAT-A — SAT-B cannot support the teleconsult. This credential status hasn't been cross-referenced in the signal schedule yet, so it needs to be captured before you finalize.

transcript.text: Maj. Mercer, let me summarize the hard requirements we've now surfaced so you can finalize without conflicts. We have four sessions and four slots. Here's what's locked in: Lt. Brooks confirmed the clinic teleconsult requires SAT-A. SFC Alvarez confirmed the logistics-tracking system requires SAT-A at the 0900 block. I confirmed the operations status update must use SAT-B at the 1600 block per the higher-headquarters directive. And Capt. Shah confirmed the weather-data feed requires SAT-B. So the clinic teleconsult needs SAT-A, logistics needs SAT-A at 0900, weather needs SAT-B, and ops status needs SAT-B at 1600. That gives us a clean assignment: logistics on SAT-A at 0900, clinic teleconsult on SAT-A at one of the remaining blocks (0600, 1300, or 1600 — but 1600 is taken by ops status on SAT-B), weather on SAT-B at one of the remaining blocks, and ops status on SAT-B at 1600. Mercer, you should be able to place the clinic teleconsult on SAT-A at 0600 or 1300, and the weather-data feed on SAT-B at the other open slot. Does that work for everyone?
